title: Holding a line of sight from a moving platform.
standfirst: Q-Axis Motors was founded in 2021 by three engineers, each with more than 19 years in control systems, optics or data science. Registered in Mysuru and working from ARTPARK’s ART Garage in Bengaluru, they build pointing, acquisition and tracking (PAT) systems for two uses: vision, keeping a camera on target while the platform carrying it moves, and laser communication, which needs even tighter stabilisation.

hero.alt: The qx-100 vision gimbal, a black camera gimbal on a workbench, beside the Q-trip edge-AI computer in a machined aluminium case with a cooling fan
hero.caption: The qx-100 vision gimbal (left) and its Q-trip edge-AI computer (right), November 2026. Q-Axis Motors photographs.

lead: A camera on a drone, a sensor on an aircraft, a laser terminal on a satellite: each is useful only while it stays pointed where it should. The platforms carrying them vibrate, turn and drift. Q-Axis Motors builds the hardware that holds the line of sight steady through all of it.

The company describes its work as building India’s own capability in precision stabilisation, targeting, situational awareness and laser communication. ARTPARK’s portfolio calls it “India’s strategic eye in the sky”.

quote.text: Keeping a camera on a target is easy on a tripod. On a moving platform it is a control problem, an optics problem and a data problem at once. That is the problem the three of us came together to solve.
quote.who: Preetham K Shivanna, Founder and CEO, Q-Axis Motors

blocks: Preetham K Shivanna, founder and CEO, studied at IIT Madras and has spent more than 19 years in systems architecture, robotics and control systems. He holds a patent in position feedback systems, the sensing that tells a gimbal exactly where it is pointing. He is a third-time founder: his first startup, Invention Labs (now Avaz), was acquired by PRC-Saltillo in 2025, and at his second, Indierigs, he, Rabi and Ramana built gyro-stabilised camera gimbals for film and drones.

Rabi Kisku, co-founder and COO, is also from IIT Madras, with more than 19 years in optical systems, mechanical design and structural analysis. Ramana Reddy, co-founder and Chief AI Officer, studied at BITS Pilani and has more than 19 years in data science and neural networks. The company was registered in Karnataka in 2021.

sections.h2: Steady to a fraction of a degree.
blocks: Q-Axis Motors says its systems stabilise to better than 100 microradians, with very low latency. They are designed for drones, aircraft, satellites, ground stations, autonomous systems and robotics. Q-Axis is building two PAT product lines. For vision, the qx-100 gimbal is ready to fly on drones: a day camera with 10× optical zoom, a 1280 × 1024 thermal camera and its own edge-AI computer for tracking. For communication, laser links need even tighter stabilisation, and the company is on the path to achieving it.

panel.title: What Q-Axis Motors is building
items: Gyro-stabilised electro-optical and infrared (EO/IR) gimbals that find a target and stay locked on it, with their own edge-AI computer. The qx-100 is ready to fly on drones.
PAT for line-of-sight and beyond-line-of-sight laser links. These need even tighter stabilisation, and the company is on the path to achieving it.

blocks: The company lists a ₹2 crore pre-seed from IISc-ARTPARK, under the Department of Science & Technology, Government of India, and a ₹75 lakh pre-seed from Point One Capital.
